english.title: Vet fail to enter details of veterinary medicinal product administered to a food producing animal in keeper's records
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a veterinary surgeon who had administered a veterinary medicinal product, namely **(..SPECIFY PRODUCT..), to a food-producing animal, as soon as reasonably practicable failed to enter the details required under regulations18 of the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..), in the keeper's records or give it to the keeper in writing
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations18, 43(j)and 44(1) of the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
This offence applies from the 17th May 2024 due to changes made by the Veterinary Medicines (Amendment etc.) Regulations 2024. For the offence applying before date, see
H18697.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
